issues.claim: The gates the pipeline fixes before the pull searches are each barred by a cited subset of law 1 that leaves out (9) and (10): S5a Trace (2)'s pin rule (l. 6600) 'a pin §2.7's laws bar ... (law 1 (1), (4), (5), read with their terms; law 2 Not yet built)'; S3 (7) (l. 6224) the gate route's re-solve trigger '(law 1 (1), (4), (5), read with their terms: ...)', the harbour gate '(a search over lawful points, §2.7's laws, law 1 (1), law 2 (a))' and the carried way's gate 'where §2.7's laws bar it there (law 1 (4), (5))'; S5b's count (l. 6650) and row (d) (l. 2916) likewise. Pins are fixed before the pull ('with the gates pinned', l. 6599-6600; 'the gates ... never moving', l. 6603; S3 (9) l. 6251), so the pull's F1 search '(law 1 (2)-(6), (9)-(11) ...)' cannot move one. Law 1 (9) (l. 2736-2738) bars a wall's line newly in a held building's strip (the span's strip widened by the wall strips' width, l. 2642-2643) and law 1 (10) (l. 2739-2743) a wall's band or strip newly across a shape-locked raised way's vault-use span. Case: at a Regenerate (keep) or New random of a CITY whose kept raised way's vault span seats a building the user locked (T110-4 (c)'s fixture class; the state sweep's C8 fourth run), the stage boundary crosses an arterial beside the raised way within the wall strips' width of that span, its footprint and band clear of the strip and the ends. Builder 1 reads the parentheses as the bar: the pin stays pinned, no shape is lawful, F-WALL's detection (l. 9852: 'a held building's widened strip ... it cannot keep clear') runs the raised-way rung alone and the stage is left unwalled; at stage 1 S3 (7) does not re-solve. Builder 2 reads 'a pin §2.7's laws bar' as all of law 1 and moves the pin by law 2 (a) (l. 2810-2813), the stage walled. Both keep law 1 and pass §5.3 and T110-4; builder 1's is a stage given way where law 2 (a) lays a lawful shape, ruled against J144 as the program reads it (PRB7H-GEN-04 (i); VF7w-GEN-01's class; adjudication-r7x.md l. 133-138 on a subset citation as a restatement gap). No valid choice.
issues.required_change: (pipeline) §4.2 S3 (7) (l. 6224): "or would put its gate where §2.7's laws admit none (law 1 (1), (4), (5), read with their terms:" -> "or would put its gate where §2.7's laws admit none (law 1 (1), (4), (5), (9), (10), read with their terms:"; the same paragraph: "(a search over lawful points, §2.7's laws, law 1 (1), law 2 (a))" -> "(a search over lawful points, §2.7's laws, law 1 (1), (4), (5), (9), (10), law 2 (a))"; and "its gate, where §2.7's laws bar it there (law 1 (4), (5)), resolved as S5a's pin is" -> "its gate, where §2.7's laws bar it there (law 1 (4), (5), (9), (10)), resolved as S5a's pin is"; §4.4 S5a Trace (2) (l. 6600): "(law 1 (1), (4), (5), read with their terms; law 2 *Not yet built*)" -> "(law 1 (1), (4), (5), (9), (10), read with their terms; law 2 *Not yet built*)"; §4.4 S5b (l. 6650): "§2.7's laws, law 1 (1), (4), (5), law 2 (a), (b), *Not yet built*" -> "§2.7's laws, law 1 (1), (4), (5), (9), (10), law 2 (a), (b), *Not yet built*". END (model, the way-and-channel table's row (d), l. 2916): "and one whose gate these laws bar where the boundary crosses it (law 1 (1), (4), (5))" -> "and one whose gate these laws bar where the boundary crosses it (law 1 (1), (4), (5), (9), (10))".

issues.claim: S5d's top-up (l. 6716-6718) has 'S5a re-traces only the affected arc between its pinned gates', naming only 'the land beyond a deck's foot the re-traced arc cannot then take moved to the next stage's quota as a moated arc's is'. E-P12 (adjudication-r7.md l. 2172-2177, PRB7C-GEN-09 l. 2999) reads the top-up as S5a's trace step run again, whose class is F-WALL (§4.1, l. 5708); F-WALL (l. 9852) runs 'a raised-way meeting ... at generation, a regeneration and a village derivation' on its own rung alone, 'the boundary re-pulled once ... -> that stage left unwalled'. S5d's own class F-BUDGET-STAGE (l. 9851) reads 'recompute the trace -> accept and report the shortfall', and law 2 (c) (l. 2827-2836) gives 'the newer structure is not built ... or, where its stage must lay it, that stage's raised-way rung'. Case: a top-up grows the boundary more than the 40 m band beyond the old arc, which must cross a standing aqueduct whose channel there runs above the ring's top by less than the deck's depth (no over or merged form, law 1 (2)), or whose only crossings lie in a held building's strip or across a shape-locked raised way's vault-use spans (law 1 (9), (10)); the old arc crossed it lawfully. Builder 1 (S5a's step, F-WALL): re-pull widened, else the stage, already walled and grown by S5c, left unwalled. Builder 2 (law 2 (c)'s first branch, F-BUDGET-STAGE, S5d's moated-arc precedent): the arc not re-traced, the old arc kept, the shortfall moved on, reported. Both keep law 1 and pass §5.3 and T110-4; builder 1 gives a stage way where a lawful wall stands (PRB7H-GEN-04 (i), as the program reads J144). No valid choice; rare, but a defined edge no bar runs.
issues.required_change: (pipeline, §4.4 S5d, l. 6718) "the land beyond a deck's foot the re-traced arc cannot then take moved to the next stage's quota as a moated arc's is, reported," -> "the land beyond a deck's foot the re-traced arc cannot then take moved to the next stage's quota as a moated arc's is, reported, and an arc §2.7's laws give no lawful shape against a standing raised way within its search band not re-traced — the arc kept as it stood and its shortfall moved to the next stage's quota as a moated arc's is, reported (F-BUDGET-STAGE; §2.7's laws, law 2 (c): the newer structure not built), F-WALL's raised-way rung never run on a top-up —,". END (determinism, §5.2 F-WALL, l. 9852): "**A raised-way meeting** (the detection's last clause), at generation, a regeneration and a village derivation, takes its own rung alone" -> "**A raised-way meeting** (the detection's last clause), at generation, a regeneration and a village derivation — but a top-up's re-trace, which §4.4 S5d keeps as it stood —, takes its own rung alone".

issues.claim: A merged polycentric pair's cross wall (§4.2 S3 (6), l. 6219-6222: 'a cross wall along T's partition line between them ... with a gate where the inter-nucleus route crosses it') is a wall line dated S3 (6), while the inter-nucleus route is one of (5)'s routes ('a polycentric pair gate to gate', l. 6196; §4.3 Routes l. 6420-6422) whose raised stretches are dated S3 (7) (Order, l. 2679-2682). Law 1 (3) (l. 2716-2720) lets a road deck cross only a run fixed after it, and law 1 (1) (l. 2702-2704) puts no gate on a deck. S3 (7) (l. 6224) re-solves a route only where its first point at T = t_1 is barred, excluding 'every deck edge whose ends straddle the stage-1 boundary', and leaves the other stretches standing 'so that (9)'s pull keeps off their deck lines (law 1 (3))'; §4.3 Where it may not go (l. 6500) counts only 'the stage-1 boundary — from S3 (9) on, its trace' as standing at S3 (7). Part P's probe tables (probe-r7f-gen l. 405, -r7g-gen l. 349, -r7h-gen l. 368) record the laws' outcome — '(a): the route re-solved so its deck comes down before the cross wall ... through its gate beyond the foot; else F-ROUTE' — but no pipeline text carries it. Case: a twin-town or polycentric CITY merged across a ravine, the inter-nucleus route priced on a viaduct across the partition line. Builder 1 (the text): the cross wall on its line crosses a later deck line (law 1 (3) broken, E_INVARIANT) or, read on the deck, takes a gate there (law 1 (1)); pulled at (9), it keeps off the deck line, crosses the route's ground beyond a foot only within its 40 m band, else F-WALL's raised-way rung, else stage 1 unwalled. Builder 2 (the laws): the S3 (7)-dated stretch is the newer and is re-solved by law 2 (a) to come down before the cross wall. R7-03 (a)'s class (VPC-r6-01, major), the stage-1 boundary's twin.
issues.required_change: (pipeline) §4.2 S3 (7) (l. 6224): "A route whose first point at `T = t_1` lies on a raised stretch of its solved course" -> "A route whose first point at `T = t_1` — or, for a merged pair's inter-nucleus route, whose crossing of the cross wall's line ((6)) — lies on a raised stretch of its solved course"; the same sentence: "every deck edge whose ends straddle the stage-1 boundary, or with an end nearer the boundary than the first point beyond the foot there" -> "every deck edge whose ends straddle the stage-1 boundary or a merged pair's cross wall, or with an end nearer either than the first point beyond the foot there"; §4.3 Where it may not go (l. 6500): "(at S3 (7) the stage-1 boundary — from S3 (9) on, its trace — and at S5b" -> "(at S3 (7) the stage-1 boundary and a merged pair's cross wall — from S3 (9) on, their trace — and at S5b".

issues.claim: S5b (l. 6650: 'its way else re-routed through a gate this step spawns') and the way-and-channel table's row (d) (l. 2916: 'else its way re-routed through a gate S5b spawns (law 2 (b))') name only spawned gates, where S5a Trace (2)'s step (b) (l. 6600) re-routes 'to cross the boundary at a gate those laws admit (a gate S5b spawned among them; ...)', and S5b spawns none when N_k <= c (l. 6653). Restatements narrower than the step they describe; S5a's step and T110-2 (3)'s third run ('through a lawful gate of the stage', l. 19372-19375) decide it, every build keeping law 1 and N_k.
issues.required_change: (pipeline, §4.4 S5b, l. 6650) "its way else re-routed through a gate this step spawns" -> "its way else re-routed as S5a *Trace* (2)'s step (b) says, through a lawful gate of the stage (one this step spawns among them)". END (model, row (d), l. 2916): "else its way re-routed through a gate S5b spawns (law 2 (b))" -> "else its way re-routed through a lawful gate of the stage, one S5b spawns among them (law 2 (b))".

issues.claim: §4.1's batch table names no write for the re-routes law 2 (b) now makes at generation — S5a Trace (2)'s step (b) for an arterial or a carried way (l. 6600) and S3 (7)'s (b) for a carried way at stage 1 (l. 6224), each re-laying a standing L1 way. The S5 row (l. 5708) gives 'k = 1 — S5a L1: S3's trace with its gate vertices' and 'S5a L1: the trace with every arterial crossing on ground part 0, and a carried way's lawful pin, as a gate'; S3's row writes no way at L1. A list omitting a write its rule names; the outcome is the laws' in every build.
issues.required_change: (pipeline, §4.1's S5 row, l. 5708) "k = 1 — S5a L1: S3's trace with its gate vertices" -> "k = 1 — S5a L1: S3's trace with its gate vertices, a carried way §4.2 S3 (7) re-routes by §2.7's laws, law 2 (b), re-laid in it"; and "and a carried way's lawful pin, as a gate (§4.4 S5a *Trace* (2));" -> "and a carried way's lawful pin, as a gate, an arterial or carried way §4.4 S5a *Trace* (2)'s step (b) re-routes re-laid in the same batch between its nearest unmoved nodes (§2.7's laws, law 2 (b));".

issues.claim: S3 (10) (l. 6289) lays a carried way's gate deck 'where ... the carried way crosses the channel, perpendicular to it', and S5a Outer moats (l. 6633-6637) decks a carried way 'as at stage 1', its bank vertices 'on its arterial or carried way where a wet stretch's banks will cross it'; but the re-route that brings a way onto a perpendicular deck is stated only for S4's solved routes (§4.3 Routes, l. 6413-6416) and 'the arterial' (l. 6636). A carried way meeting its moat more than 10° off the normal: (i) its stretch re-routed between its gate and its next node beyond the channel, its deck perpendicular, as an arterial's; or (ii) its deck laid where the banks cross it, oblique, the way unmoved. Both keep law 1 and Carried way's gate; T110-2 (6)'s fifth run (l. 19593-19596) passes both; §4.3's ±10° deck bar runs on B-CITY, which holds no carried way.
issues.required_change: Pick (i), which S3 (10)'s 'perpendicular' already asks: (pipeline, §4.4 S5a Outer moats, l. 6636-6637) "(the arterial is re-routed between the gate and its next pinned node beyond the channel" -> "(the arterial or carried way is re-routed between the gate and its next pinned node beyond the channel"; (§4.3 Routes, l. 6413-6414) "Where S3 carved water across a solved route — the city moat just outside each gate — S4 re-solves only that stretch," -> "Where S3 carved water across a solved route or a carried way standing before the stage — the city moat just outside each gate, §4.2 S3 (10) — S4 re-solves only that stretch,". Else list for fix-list.md: "base §4.2 S3 (10), §4.4 S5a Outer moats: a carried way meeting its gate's moat deck more than 10° off the channel's normal — re-routed through a perpendicular deck as an arterial is, or decked where the banks cross it, the way unmoved; the builder picks one."
